6:43.sourceText: καὶ ἦραν κλάσματα δώδεκα κοφίνων πληρώματα καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰχθύων.
6:43.targetText: and they took up of broken pieces twelve hand-baskets full, and of the fishes,

groups.note: The Greek broken-pieces object is rendered as English partitive of broken pieces, with no separate source of preposition.

6:44.sourceText: καὶ ἦσαν οἱ φαγόντες τοὺς ἄρτους πεντακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες.
6:44.targetText: and those eating of the loaves were about five thousand men.

groups.note: Greek aorist participle those who ate is rendered eating in LSV; the eating event remains shared.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an approximate about to the number; N1904 gives five thousand without an approximation word.

6:45.sourceText: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν εἰς τὸ πέραν πρὸς Βηθσαϊδάν, ἕως αὐτὸς ἀπολύει τὸν ὄχλον.
6:45.targetText: And immediately He constrained His disciples to go into the boat, and to go before [Him] to the other side, to Bethsaida, until He may let the multitude away,

groups.note: Greek present releases is rendered may let ... away under the English until clause; the same release predicate is retained.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English object of go before is supplied; N1904 has no separate Him with the preceding verb.

6:46.sourceText: καὶ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.
6:46.targetText: and having taken leave of them, He went away to the mountain to pray.

6:47.sourceText: καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ αὐτὸς μόνος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
6:47.targetText: And evening having come, the boat was in the midst of the sea, and He alone on the land;

6:48.sourceText: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτοὺς βασανιζομένους ἐν τῷ ἐλαύνειν, ἦν γὰρ ὁ ἄνεμος ἐναντίος αὐτοῖς, περὶ τετάρτην φυλακὴν τῆς νυκτὸς ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης· καὶ ἤθελεν παρελθεῖν αὐτούς.
6:48.targetText: and He saw them harassed in the rowing, for the wind was against them, and about the fourth watch of the night He comes to them walking on the sea, and wished to pass by them.

groups.note: Greek seeing participle is rendered as a finite He saw clause in LSV.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV inserts an additional and before about the fourth watch; N1904 proceeds directly from the wind explanation to the time phrase.

6:49.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἔδοξαν ὅτι φάντασμά ἐστιν, καὶ ἀνέκραξαν·
6:49.targetText: And they having seen Him walking on the sea, thought [it] to be an apparition, and cried out,

groups.note: Greek that it is is recast as the English thought-it-to-be infinitival complement; the complementizer and copula share that clausal construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English infinitival subject supplied in thought it to be; Greek encodes the third-person subject in the copula without a separate it pronoun.

6:50.sourceText: πάντες γὰρ αὐτὸν εἶδαν καὶ ἐταράχθησαν. ὁ δὲ εὐθὺς ἐλάλησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
6:50.targetText: for they all saw Him, and were troubled, and immediately He spoke with them, and says to them, “Take courage! I AM; do not be afraid.”

6:51.sourceText: καὶ ἀνέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος· καὶ λίαν ἐκ περισσοῦ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἐξίσταντο·
6:51.targetText: And He went up to them into the boat, and the wind stilled, and greatly out of measure they were amazed in themselves, and were wondering,

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes an additional wondering predicate and conjunction after amazed; these words are absent from pinned N1904.

6:52.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ συνῆκαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄρτοις, ἀλλ’ ἦν αὐτῶν ἡ καρδία πεπωρωμένη.
6:52.targetText: for they did not understand concerning the loaves, for their heart has been hard.

groups.note: Greek was with a perfect passive hardened participle denotes the hardened heart state; LSV renders has been hard. The copula and hardening/state predicate share the whole English construction.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness connective difference: N1904 contrasts with but, ἀλλά, while LSV gives causal for. These unlike connectors are left unpaired.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has causal for where N1904 has contrasting but; the initial Greek for stays linked to the initial English for.

6:53.sourceText: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἦλθον εἰς Γεννησαρὲτ καὶ προσωρμίσθησαν.
6:53.targetText: And having passed over, they came on the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore,

groups.note: Greek movement into Gennesaret is expressed in LSV as the land of Gennesaret; the named-place phrase is retained with its directional-to-modifying construction change explicit.

6:54.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν
6:54.targetText: and they having come forth out of the boat, immediately having recognized Him,

6:55.sourceText: περιέδραμον ὅλην τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ ἤρξαντο ἐπὶ τοῖς κραβάττοις τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας περιφέρειν, ὅπου ἤκουον ὅτι ἐστίν.
6:55.targetText: they ran around through all that surrounding region, and they began to carry around on the pallets those being ill, where they were hearing that He is,

groups.note: The Greek ran-around verb takes the traversed region directly; English adds through within the same path-of-motion predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes surrounding as a region modifier; N1904 has the plain region noun without a surrounding modifier.

6:56.sourceText: καὶ ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο εἰς κώμας ἢ εἰς πόλεις ἢ εἰς ἀγροὺς, ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἐτίθεσαν τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα κἂν τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἂν ἥψαντο αὐτοῦ ἐσῴζοντο.
6:56.targetText: and wherever He was going, to villages, or cities, or fields, in the marketplaces they were laying the ailing, and were calling on Him, that they may touch if it were but the fringe of His garment, and as many as were touching Him were saved.

groups.note: Greek repeats the preposition before villages, cities and fields; English uses a single shared to for all three destinations.
The contracted κἄν supplies the even-if/if-only minimum-contact condition, expanded by LSV as if it were but. No separate Greek it or were is invented.
